title: Transparent span enrichment and compact propagator shim
creator: Aisha Kaur
description:
Context:
We need a lightweight, backwards-compatible instrumentation shim that enriches spans with platform metadata and uses a compact, network-friendly propagation header for high-throughput services (edge proxies, gateways, and mobile SDKs). Existing OpenTelemetry propagation is feature-complete but often verbose and brittle for high-QPS paths; we want a small footprint alternative that falls back to OTEL when available and preserves correlation for downstream services and Redwood Console dashboards.

Goals:
- Provide a single, compact trace propagation header (span-context + small baggage) that fits common HTTP header size constraints and is safe through proxies and CDNs.
- Attach deterministic span enrichment hooks at the SDK/middleware boundary (Node/Python/Go) to add non-sensitive platform attributes (customer_id hash, model_variant, queue_wait_ms) for diagnostics and SLO dashboards.
- Preserve full compatibility with OpenTelemetry: when a full OTEL header is present, prefer it and mirror the compact header.
- Make the shim opt-out per-route and configurable via environment / SDK options.

Design decisions and trade-offs:
- Header format: we propose a base64url-encoded compact blob in header name "x-rw-ctx" containing trace_id(16B):span_id(8B):flags(1B):baggage_kv_pairs (length-prefixed, limited to 128 bytes). This keeps most requests under typical header size limits and avoids comma-separated baggage fragility.
- Sampling propagation: include a single sampled flag; when sampling decisions change mid-request (eg. dynamic sampler), the shim will attach a secondary header "x-rw-sample-hint" to communicate the new decision for downstream observability.
- Enrichment policy: SDK middleware will enrich spans with a fixed allowlist of attributes only (no user PII). List: customer_hash, route_id, model_variant, config_profile, queue_wait_ms, inference_tokens. This list is immutable by default but configurable at initialization time for platform teams.
- OTEL compatibility: if OTEL headers (traceparent/tracestate or otel header) exist, the shim will read and mirror the trace/span ids into x-rw-ctx; when both exist, we tag a span attribute shim.mirrored_from = "otel".
- Backpressure & performance: enrichment should be async and bounded — heavy operations (DB lookups, KMS calls) must not run in request path. We will only use in-memory / cacheable values; any long-lived enrichment will be provided by a background metadata cache service (see dependencies).

Implementation plan / milestones:
1) Prototype header encoder/decoder and unit tests (Node) — 2d.
2) Node SDK middleware + route opt-out flag + unit and integration tests with local gateway — 3d.
3) Python and Go shims (feature-parity) — 4d.
4) Mirror behavior with OTEL and add fallback logic — 2d.
5) Telemetry and dashboards: emit internal metrics: shim.encode.latency, shim.decode.latency, shim.decode.errors, shim.baggage-truncated.count. Add logs when baggage truncated or invalid. — 2d.
6) End-to-end QA and canary on internal services (edge-proxy, inference-api) with rollout plan — 3d.

Acceptance criteria (must pass for Done):
- Unit test coverage for encoder/decoder across edge cases (malformed header, truncated baggage, cross-language roundtrip).
- Middleware implemented in Node/Python/Go with config flag to enable/disable enrichment per route.
- No observable p95 latency increase > 1ms for instrumented services in canary.
- Shim emits metrics (shim.encode.latency, shim.decode.latency, shim.decode.errors, shim.baggage-truncated.count) to metrics pipeline and shows up in staging Grafana dashboard.
- OTEL compatibility verified: when OTEL headers present, trace IDs are preserved and Console traces join correctly.
- Security review signed off for header format and enrichment allowlist.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: header different from community standards may confuse external integrators. Mitigation: provide adapter that reads/writes W3C traceparent when requested and document interoperability.
- Risk: baggage size growth causing upstream proxy rejections. Mitigation: enforce 128-byte total baggage limit and drop oldest entries with a metric emitted.
- Risk: accidental PII enrichment. Mitigation: enrichment allowlist is restricted and reviewed as part of security checklist; runtime will redact anything matching PII patterns.

Monitoring & rollout:
- Initial canary: 5% traffic on edge-proxy -> observe shim.decode.errors and p95 latency for 48h.
- If errors < 0.05% and latency regression < 1ms, increase to 25% then 100% over a week.
- Dashboard: create temporary Grafana panel group under Observability / Tracing / Shim that surfaces encode/decode latencies, error rate, and baggage truncation count. Link: https://grafana.internal.redwood/r/observability-shim (staging).
